key_insight: ARMOR++ makes black-box transfer attacks on deepfake detectors more effective by using an agentic, multi-domain primitive set that better preserves transferable forensic cues across model architectures. In simple terms, it turns attack generation into a coordinated multi-agent process instead of relying on a single brittle surrogate.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the drop in attack success when adversarial examples are transferred from one deepfake detector to another, especially under no-query constraints and when moving from convolutional surrogates to transformer-based targets.
method: Uses a multi-agent orchestration framework to coordinate attack generation across complementary roles.
Builds attacks from a multi-domain primitive set to improve semantic awareness and transferability.
Optimizes perturbations for black-box settings, aiming to remain effective without querying the target model.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners working on security and robustness, ARMOR++ highlights a stronger threat model for deepfake detectors and shows that transfer attacks can be improved through structured orchestration. It can inform both red-teaming workflows and the design of more resilient detection systems.

paper_title: ARMOR++: Agentic Orchestration of a Multi-Domain Primitive Set for Transferable Attacks on Deepfake Detectors
paper_authors: Christos Korgialas, Gabriel Lee Jun Rong, Dion Jia Xu Ho, Pai Chet Ng, Xiaoxiao Miao
